## How they got there
Liverpool finished as runner-up after losing the final to Real Madrid 0-1. Their profile during the group and league phase was defined by exceptional efficiency, ranking better than 97% of teams in points per game with a value of 3.0, while also beating 97% of peers in shot accuracy at 59.2%. They further distinguished themselves by surpassing 97% of teams in possession percentage, recording a value of 59.5%, which established them as a dominant force throughout the campaign.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model assigned Liverpool a 32.5% probability of reaching the final, significantly higher than the 12.5% base rate for a random knockout team. With a rank of 2 among all season's participants, the system identified them as one of only two teams it would select to reach the final stage. Consequently, the model's expectation aligned with the semi-finals, indicated by an expected stage value of 2.24 on its scale.

## Weak spots
The team's lowest rankings appeared in distance covered per game at 113.1 km, where they were better than only 25% of teams, and fouls committed per game with a value of 12.0, beating just 38%. Although the model marked down fouls committed as a negative factor for their progression, Liverpool still ranked better than 48% of all Champions League teams since 2011-12 on this metric despite the statistical association working against them.

messages.content: You are a football performance analyst writing for a curious, data-literate reader. Use ONLY the facts provided. Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events, analyses or numbers that are not in the facts. 'Better than this %' figures say how many teams the club beat on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where beating a team means having the lower value. Write them as 'better than X% of teams', never as 'top X%'. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat or a team's profile drove, powered, propelled, carried, helped, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Write plain markdown without tables.
